title: Bonk's Adventure
subtitle: A caveman leads with his head
summary: Bonk's Adventure is the prehistoric platform game released as PC Genjin for Japan's PC Engine on 15 December 1989.
body: Bonk's Adventure is the prehistoric platform game released as PC Genjin for Japan's PC Engine on 15 December 1989. Bonk travels to rescue Princess Za from King Drool, confronting cartoon dinosaurs with his oversized forehead. Jumping into a head-first attack gives the character a distinctive way to move and fight. The broad expressions and exaggerated bodies make that action easy to understand: this is a platform hero whose strongest feature is also the center of his visual personality.

Fruit and vegetables restore Bonk's hearts, while meat temporarily increases his power. A smaller piece grants an intermediate state, and a large piece can take him directly to an invulnerable form. The changing state affects the next confrontation and gives food a purpose beyond collecting points. A head-first landing can stun enemies through the ground, extending the attack beyond direct contact. The player learns to combine a jump, the direction of Bonk's body and the remaining power-up time when approaching the next group of creatures.

Red Company created the characters and designed the original game, Atlus handled much of its development, and A.I contributed background work under Hudson's supervision. The Japanese name PC Genjin plays on PC Engine itself; European audiences encountered the character as PC Kid or B.C. Kid. The North American release arrived in 1990. Bonk became closely associated with the system before appearing on other platforms, carrying a recognizable comic personality through an unusually direct connection between character design and the action performed on screen.
